title: SpaceX Gets the Go-Ahead for Satellites That Power AI in Space
summary:
SpaceX has won approval for a new idea: data centres in space. On Wednesday, US regulators said the company, owned by Elon Musk, may launch up to a million satellites into orbit around Earth. The project is called Starmind, and it is the first approval of its kind.

The satellites would use sunlight for power. They would process data for artificial intelligence, or AI, and send results back to Earth. SpaceX says space data centres are the cheapest way to meet the growing demand for AI computing power. The FCC said the project would help America's fast-growing AI economy.

Not everyone is cheering. Amazon called the plan more of a grand ambition than a realistic plan. Astronomers said it would seriously harm people's ability to study the night sky. The American Astronomical Society said it was deeply disappointed.

SpaceX wants to launch its first Starmind satellite next year. But it is unclear whether a million satellites will really be launched. Like Starlink, which already uses more than 10,000 satellites, they would fly 500 to 2,000 kilometres above Earth.
why_it_matters: The night sky you see could change if thousands more satellites fill it, and the computers behind your apps could move into space.
